why_standalone: A real-data replication and forecasting study (Polity5 and Seshat Cliopatria) for research track 24 (civ); it tests published claims (Arbesman 2011, Gates et al. 2006) and supplies the empirical lifespans that civ-levers' simulated civilizations are to be checked against.
title: How long do regimes, states and empires last, and does the risk of collapse rise or fall with age?
summary: Survival analysis of 1,387 Polity5 regime spells (1800–2018) and 1,543 named states and empires in Seshat’s Cliopatria (3400 BCE–2024, CC BY). Regimes age out of risk: the yearly chance a spell ends peaks at 12% in years 2–5 and falls to 2% after age 80; for democracies to 0.5% after age 40, while anocracies and autocracies level off near 5%. Anocracies end 1.9× as fast as democracies (95% CI 1.6–2.2), replicating Gates et al. (2006). Fitted only on data before each cutoff (1966–2006), a piecewise hazard by type and age forecasts which regimes end within 10 years with AUC 0.69 over 696 forecasts and beats a constant-hazard baseline on Brier score (0.222 against 0.252), though every model forecast fewer endings than happened. For empires that ever held a million km² the Weibull shape is 0.91 (CI 0.82–1.02), consistent with Arbesman’s (2011) memoryless lifetimes; across all polities there is high early risk (1.1%/year in the first 25 years) then about 46% a century, and starting bigger does not help (hazard ratio 1.06 per tenfold area). Over a century, age barely predicts which states survive (within-cutoff AUC 0.46–0.61): the turnover rate of the era (35% a century after 1600, 79% after 1900) dominates. Applied to today: 41% of 2018 regimes expected to end by 2028 (young anocracies about 70%, long-standing full democracies 5–7%), and about half of today’s mapped states expected to persist under the same name to 2124, within a backtest range of 0.2–0.65. A Polity “regime end” is any 3-point change, not a collapse; the models use only type and age, so the probabilities are base rates, not judgements about any country.
lede: how long do regimes, states and empires last? On Polity5 (1,387 regimes since 1800) and Seshat's Cliopatria (1,543 polities since 3400 BCE), regimes age out of risk (democracies to 0.5% a year after 40 years, anocracies stay near 5%), big empires fit a constant hazard (Arbesman 2011), and a backtested duration model forecasts 10-year regime change with AUC 0.69; applied to 2018's regimes and 2024's states
